dhpak2.6:1.1: 2.6 The Story about Two Bhikkhu Friends, One Heedful and One Heedless
dhpak2.6:2.1: “Heedful amongst the heedless ones,” {1.260} this Dhamma teaching was given by
dhpak2.6:2.2: the Teacher while he was in residence at Jetavana with reference to two friends.
dhpak2.6:3.1: It appears that these two bhikkhus obtained a subject of meditation from the Teacher and went forth to a forest hermitage.
dhpak2.6:3.2: Early in the morning one of them brought firewood, prepared the charcoal-dish,
dhpak2.6:3.3: and during the first watch sat warming himself and chatting with the young novices.
dhpak2.6:3.4: The other, a heedful bhikkhu, engaged in the practice of a renunciant, thus admonished his friend:
dhpak2.6:3.5: “Friend, do not act thus. For a heedless bhikkhu the four lower realms are as if they were his own house.
dhpak2.6:3.6: The favor of the Buddhas may not be won by double-dealing.”
dhpak2.6:3.7: When the lazy bhikkhu paid no attention to his admonition, the
dhpak2.6:3.8: heedful bhikkhu said: “This bhikkhu cannot endure to be spoken to.”
dhpak2.6:3.9: Without speaking to him further, the heedful bhikkhu continued his practice. {1.261}
dhpak2.6:4.1: The slothful elder, having warmed himself during the first watch,
dhpak2.6:4.2: entered just as his friend, having finished his walk, entered his cell.
dhpak2.6:4.3: The slothful bhikkhu said to the heedful bhikkhu: “Slothful one, you entered the forest for
dhpak2.6:4.4: the purpose of lying down and sleeping. Seeing that you obtained a subject of meditation from
dhpak2.6:4.5: the Buddhas, ought you not rather to rise and devote yourself to the practice of a renunciant?”
dhpak2.6:4.6: So saying, he entered his own place of residence, lay down, and went to sleep.
dhpak2.6:4.7: But his friend, after resting during the second watch, rose in
dhpak2.6:4.8: the last watch and devoted himself to the practice of a renunciant.
dhpak2.6:4.9: Living thus the life of heedfulness, in no long time he attained Arahatship, [28.313] together with the analytic knowledges.
dhpak2.6:4.10: The other bhikkhu, however, spent his time in utter heedlessness.
dhpak2.6:5.1: When the two bhikkhus had completed the rains retreat, they went to
dhpak2.6:5.2: the Teacher, worshipped him, and sat down respectfully on one side.
dhpak2.6:5.3: The Teacher exchanged friendly greetings with them and queried: “I trust that you have
dhpak2.6:5.4: lived the life of heedfulness and that you have devoted yourselves earnestly to the
dhpak2.6:5.5: practice of a renunciant. I trust that you have reached the goal of the spiritual life.”
dhpak2.6:5.6: The heedless bhikkhu replied: “Venerable Sir, how can this bhikkhu be said to
dhpak2.6:5.7: be heedful? From the time he left you he has done nothing but lie and sleep.”
dhpak2.6:5.9: – “I, venerable Sir, betimes in the morning brought firewood and prepared the
dhpak2.6:5.10: charcoal-dish, and during the first watch I sat and warmed myself, but I did not spend my time sleeping.”
dhpak2.6:6.1: Then said the Teacher to the slothful bhikkhu: “You who have spent your time
dhpak2.6:6.2: in heedlessness say: ‘I am heedful.’ You call the heedful one heedless.” {1.262}
dhpak2.6:8.1: “Compared with my son, you are like a weak horse that has lost its speed; but he,
dhpak2.6:8.2: compared with you, is like a swift horse.” So saying, he pronounced the following verse:
dhpak2.6:9.1: Heedful amongst the heedless ones, wakeful amongst the ones who sleep,
dhpak2.6:9.2: like a swift horse who abandons a weak horse, the true sage moves on.
dhpak2.6:11.1: At the conclusion of the verse many reached the fruition of Stream-entry and so on.
